items.title: Section: Five Practices That Actually Draw Forth What a King Truly Wants

items.zh: 一、恩養世間，二、英勇具足，三、善權方便，四、正受境界，五、勤修法行。云何名王恩養世間？謂有國王，性本知足，於財寶門為性謹慎，不邪貪著，如其所應積集財寶，不廣營求。又有國王，性無貪悋，成就無貪白淨之法，以自所有庫藏珍財，隨力隨能，給施一切貧窮孤露。又有國王，柔和忍辱，多以軟言曉諭國界；於時時間，隨其所應分賞爵祿；終不以彼非所能業、惡業、重業役任群臣；諸有違犯可矜恕罪，即便矜恕，諸有違犯不可恕罪，以實、以時如理治罰。如是名王以正化法恩養世間。由王受行如是恩養世間法故，遂感世間之所敬愛。云何名王英勇具足？謂有國王，計策無惰，武略圓滿；未降伏者而降伏之，已降伏者而攝護之；廣營事業，如前乃至不甚耽樂博弈戲等；又善觀察應與不應與，勤於僚庶，應刑罰者正刑罰之，應攝養者正攝養之。如是名王英勇具足。由王受行如是英勇具足法故，遂能感得自在增上。
items.en: First, nurturing the world with kindness. Second, possessing full heroic capability. Third, skilful expedient means. Fourth, properly enjoying sense objects. Fifth, diligently practising the Dharma. What is called a king's nurturing the world with kindness? A king naturally content, cautious with wealth, not greedily attached, accumulating only what is proper. A king free of greed and stinginess, giving according to his own means to the poor and orphaned from his own treasury. A king gentle and patient, admonishing with kind words, rewarding proportionately, never assigning tasks beyond their ability, evil tasks, or heavy tasks, forgiving forgivable faults, justly punishing unforgivable ones at the proper time. This is called nurturing the world through correct governance. Through practising this, a king comes to be loved by the world. What is called a king's full heroic capability? A king diligent in strategy, accomplished in military affairs, subduing the unconquered and protecting the submitted, skilfully managing enterprise without indulging in gambling, correctly discerning what to grant, correctly punishing and correctly caring for. This is called full heroic capability. Through practising this, a king comes to enjoy increasing sovereign authority.

items.title: Section: Eating Alone Is a Fault Even for a King

items.zh: 云何名王善權方便？謂有國王，於應和好所作所成機務等事，如前乃至於應攝受大力朋黨所作所成機務等事，能正了知和好方便，乃至攝受強黨方便。如是名王善權方便。由王受行如是善權方便法故，遂能摧伏所有怨敵。云何名王正受境界？謂有國王，善能籌量府庫增減，不奢不悋，平等自處，清正受用、眾雜受用、勝妙受用、隨其時候所宜受用、與諸臣佐親屬受用、在於勝處而為受用、奏諸伎樂而為受用、無有愆失而為受用。無愆失者，謂疾惱時，應食所宜，避所不宜；於康豫時，消已方食。若食未消，或食而利，皆不應食。應共食者正現在前，不應獨食精妙上味，詭擯餘人。
items.en: What is called a king's skilful expedient means? A king who correctly understands how to handle matters calling for conciliation, and so on through matters calling for drawing in powerful factions, correctly grasping the appropriate means in each case. This is called skilful expedient means. Through practising this, a king comes to overcome all his enemies. What is called a king's proper enjoyment of sense objects? A king who wisely gauges his own treasury's rise and fall, neither extravagant nor stingy, remaining evenly balanced, enjoying purely, variously, excellently, according to season, together with ministers and family, in fitting places, to the accompaniment of music, and without fault. Freedom from fault means eating what is suitable during illness and avoiding what is not; once recovered, eating further only once what came before has digested. Food not yet digested, or food that passes through too quickly, should not be eaten. When others ought properly to share the meal, one should genuinely share it with them, not selfishly consuming the finest food alone while contriving to exclude others.

items.title: Section: Five Qualities of Genuine Dharma Practice, and a Quick Awakening From One's Own Lapse

items.zh: 由王受行如是正受境界法故，遂能善巧攝養自身。云何名王勤修法行？謂有國王，具足淨信、戒、聞、捨、慧。云何名王具足淨信？謂有國王，信解他世，信解當來淨不淨業，及愛非愛果與異熟。如是名王具足淨信。云何名王具足淨戒？謂有國王，遠離殺生及不與取、婬欲邪行、妄語、飲酒諸放逸處。如是名王具足淨戒。云何名王具足淨聞？謂有國王，於現法義、於後法義，及於現法後法等義眾妙法門，善聽善受，習誦通利，專意研究，善見善達。如是名王具足淨聞。云何名王具足淨捨？謂有國王，雖在慳垢所纏眾中，心恒清淨，遠離慳垢，而處居家常行棄捨，舒手樂施，好興祠福，惠捨圓滿，於布施時常樂平等。如是名王具足淨捨。云何名王具足淨慧？謂有國王，如實了知善不善法、有罪無罪、修與不與、勝劣黑白，於廣分別諸緣生法亦如實知；縱令失念，生惡貪欲、瞋恚、忿、恨、覆、惱、慳、嫉、幻誑、諂曲、無慚、無愧、惡欲、惡見，而心覺悟，並不堅住。如是名王具足淨慧。如是名王勤修法行。由王受行此法行故，能往善趣。
items.en: Through practising proper enjoyment of sense objects, a king skilfully maintains his own health. What is called a king's diligent Dharma practice? A king possessing pure faith, precepts, learning, giving, and wisdom. Pure faith is believing in future lives, and in the future ripening of pure and impure deeds into desirable and undesirable results. Pure precepts is remaining free of killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and intoxicated heedlessness. Pure learning is thoroughly listening to, receiving, studying, and investigating every wondrous teaching of present and future benefit. Pure giving is, even amid those bound by miserliness, keeping one's mind constantly pure, freely giving while yet a householder, delighting in merit, giving fully with an equal heart. Pure wisdom is genuinely knowing the wholesome and unwholesome, the blameworthy and blameless, and dependent origination in full, and, even upon losing mindfulness and generating greed, hatred, and the rest, quickly becoming aware and not remaining fixed there. This is called diligent Dharma practice. Through practising this, one reaches the fortunate destinies.

items.zh: 如是五種能引發王可愛之法，能引諸王現法、後法所有利益。謂初四種能引發王現法利益，最後一種能引發王後法利益。

blocks.text: Five practises that bring a king what he wants, ending with the practice of the Dharma itself.

Master Cháng Bǎi: by not coveting wealth, giving to the poor, and rewarding and punishing rightly, the king gains the love of the world. Courage brings mastery; skilful means, not courage, overcomes enemies. The king does not ask ministers to do what they cannot, what is evil, or work that is too heavy. What cannot be forgiven he punishes according to the facts, in proportion.

Master Cháng Bǎi: when the treasury is full he is not extravagant; when short, he does not begrudge what is necessary. Eating alone, without sharing, is a fault even for a king. In illness, eat what is suitable; if earlier food is not yet digested, do not eat more.

Faith, precepts, learning, giving, and wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: faith means believing in a next life and in karma; and wisdom includes noticing at once when one lapses, waking up, and correcting it. (Untranslated, 0641c24: the first four bring benefit in this life; the last brings benefit in the next.)
Even for a king, the treatise's advice about food is practical: share it, and don't eat before the last meal is digested.

quiz.q: Which pairing of cause and beloved quality is correct?
options: heroism overcomes enemies and expedient means brings mastery, as common sense would pair them
heroism brings increasing mastery, and expedient means overcomes enemies
nurturing the world brings health
Dharma practice brings the world's love
quiz.why: The pairing is not the obvious one: heroism brings mastery, while expedient means, not heroism, overcomes enemies. Master Cháng Bǎi: thereby the king gains the beloved result of increasing mastery. Nurturing leads to love, enjoyment to health, Dharma to good destinies.

quiz.q: Which three things make up nurturing the world, in Master Cháng Bǎi's summary?
options: expanding territory, raising the population, and cutting taxes, which is what people truly need
not coveting wealth, giving to the poor, and instructing with fair rewards and penalties, which wins the world's love
building temples and fasting
conquest, protection, and diligence
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: by not coveting wealth, giving to the poor, and instructing with rewards and penalties, the king gains the love of the world. Conquest and protection belong to heroism. The treatise marks the three with 又有國王.

quiz.q: This phrase is rendered "never assigning degrading tasks." What is the problem?
options: none: all three mean lowly work, covered by one word, as the lecture says
it should be "noble tasks"
役任 should be "pay"
the three are beyond ability, evil, and too heavy; the English merges them and shifts the sense
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the king does not require of ministers what they cannot do, what is evil, or work that is too heavy. None of the three means "degrading," and the English collapses a three-part list into one misleading word.

quiz.q: How is an unforgivable offence handled under nurturing the world, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: according to the true facts, at the proper time, and in line with the actual weight of the offence
pardoning everyone, for nurturing means never punishing, since penalties cost the people's love
always the death penalty
sending it abroad for trial
quiz.why: Nurturing is not leniency without limit. Master Cháng Bǎi: for what cannot be forgiven, punish according to the facts, at the right time, and in proportion to the actual weight. Forgivable offenses are forgiven at once.

quiz.q: Within proper enjoyment, what is the king's attitude towards the treasury?
options: he gauges its rise and fall, neither extravagant nor stingy, staying evenly balanced
he stores everything unused, frugality being the highest virtue of all
he spends freely to show power
he leaves it to ministers
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when the treasury is full he is not extravagant, and when it is short he does not begrudge necessary spending. Proper enjoyment lies between extravagance and miserliness, and is measured against what the treasury can actually bear.

quiz.q: 正受境界 is rendered "properly enjoying circumstances." What does 境界 refer to, per the lecture?
options: a stage of meditation, so it should be "meditative attainment," as the lecture states
the objects enjoyed, such as food, which "circumstances" fails to convey
the national border
the king's birth situation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi's explanation turns on food: eat what is suitable during illness and avoid what is not. 境界 is thus what is enjoyed. The word "circumstances" does not show this, and §19's "agreeable objects" shows the rendering is inconsistent.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain that one should not eat when food is undigested or passes through?
options: food that brings benefit should be avoided, since 利 means profit and one must not crave it
one should not eat past noon
food not yet digested, or eaten but not absorbed and quickly passed out, should not be eaten
one should eat only vegetarian food
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if what was eaten is not yet digested, or passes out quickly without being absorbed, such food should not be eaten. Here 利 means diarrhea, not profit, and the English "passes through too quickly" agrees with the lecture.

quiz.q: A king diligent in Dharma practice is complete in which five things?
options: giving, precepts, patience, diligence, and meditation
mindfulness, meditation, wisdom, diligence, and pliancy
pure faith, precepts, learning, giving, and wisdom
peace, severance, charity, war, and factions
quiz.why: The five are faith, precepts, learning, giving, and wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi on faith: believing in a next life, and that pure and impure deeds bring desirable and undesirable ripened results. Option D lists the five matters of state instead.

quiz.q: The English gives only "the wholesome and unwholesome, the blameworthy and blameless." What should a reader keep in mind?
options: the text has only two pairs and the rest came from a commentary, as the lecture says
修與不修 and 勝劣黑白 are missing, so these cannot be drawn from the English alone
善 is omitted
如實 is omitted
quiz.why: The Chinese has four pairs and the English two. Master Cháng Bǎi also explains knowing dependent origination in detail, and that on lapsing one at once knows it, wakes up, and does not stay stuck, which the English does keep.
